answer: Every epoch, each identity must submit a fresh boot attestation: a measured-boot quote proving the machine started from a known-good state, signed by its TPM. A farm that clones one golden image produces identical quotes, and the network rejects the copies. At dawn the honest agent boots once and works all day; a scripted farm would need to wander through a hundred separate boots, each on its own hardware, to fake the same. The kernel measurement cannot be edited after the fact, so the attestation is either genuine or it fails loudly.
